chapter: Trumpeters he admired and the Ellington near-miss
title: How Ellington changed every man: Al Sears, a tenor in the band, Barney Bigard
summary: Duke wrote behind each player; Al Sears sounded better there than anywhere, and Jones wondered how a featured tenor would fit a band that never featured one, praising Barney Bigard's individual clarinet.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: And especially with you, because what he did, he made a different person out of every person that came in the band.
Every man that come in that band.
Look at Ben Webster.
Look at Al Sears.
Yeah.

Al Sears sounded good there. He played a thing in there, "Happy Go Lucky," or something, and the music that he put behind him fit him, fit that tone. Al sounded better with that band than I ever heard him in my life. And he was around Buffalo at the time, you know, when we were around there.
I wasn't here then, I don't think, when he -- in fact I think Stanley and I had married and I was in England.
Oh, I see.
But I never could understand how that happened or who brought him into that band.
I can't understand it. I didn't know what was going to happen when Barney brought in a tenor, because I can remember way back there they didn't use a tenor, not for solos.
That's right.
Maybe Barney might have played some parts with it.
That's right.
So I didn't know how a tenor was going to go into that band, whether it was going to make it sound like all the other bands or not.
That's right.
See, because all the other bands featured tenor and he never featured tenor.
That's right.
Because like Barney, you know, "Lightning" on a clarinet.
Yeah.
I never heard anybody play that much clarinet now, since, you know, not like that lightening.
No. An extraordinary style.
Yeah, the style. Good God, individual. But that's what I was speaking about, individual styles, you know.
That's right.
You knew who they were, you know.
That's right.
You could take Barney and put him in Fletcher's band and you could tell that was Barney.
Sure.
Yeah, sure.
